- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the magnitude of the correction.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds prices too high for extended periods after peaks.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the medium term (5–10 days) — suggests model lacks dynamic adjustment to recent volatility.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day window — e.g., consistent downward trend after mid-2024 prices.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks — e.g., sudden drops after high peaks are not fully reflected in forecasts.
